1.note: The pronoun **he** refers to the man with the measuring reed who was guiding Ezekiel through the temple area. It may be helpful to clarify this for your readers. Alternate translation: [And the man with the measuring reed brought me]

The **nave** was a kind of large main room in the temple building, which people entered from the porch. It is also called the Holy Place. If your readers would not be familiar with what a nave is, you could use the name of a similar thing that your readers would recognize, or you could use a more general term. See the Introduction to this chapter for more information. Alternate translation: [the large main room of the temple]

These **cubits** were a unit of measurement corresponding to the distance between an average person’s elbow and middle fingertip, or about 46 centimeters or 18 inches. The cubits that the man used were each one handbreadth longer than the common cubit, so each one was about 54 centimeters or 21 inches, and **six cubits** was about 3.2 meters or 10.5 feet. If it would be helpful to your readers, you could express these measurements in modern measurements, either in the text or a footnote. This is the length of the cubit that Ezekiel uses throughout this section. Alternate translation: [about 3.2 meters or 10.5 feet]

1.q: שֵׁשׁ אַמּ֨וֹת רֹ֧חַב מִ⁠פּ֛וֹ וְ⁠שֵׁשׁ אַמּֽוֹת רֹ֥חַב מִ⁠פּ֖וֹ
1.note: Ezekiel is using **from here** and **from there** to mean “on each side.” You could indicate this explicitly in your translation if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [six cubits in width on each side]

The phrase translated as **the width of the tent** represents the standard written Hebrew text as we have it today. This reading, however, does not seem to make sense. Scholars have proposed that a scribe may have added these words in explanation in the margin, and then someone else added it into the verse by accident. Most translations do not include this phrase. The UST follows that interpretation. You may want to follow the major translation in your area.

2.note: Ezekiel is using **the shoulders of** as a common expression of the culture to mean “the sides of.” If this phrase does not have that meaning for your readers, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [and the side walls of the opening]

2.q: חָמֵ֤שׁ אַמּוֹת֙ מִ⁠פּ֔וֹ וְ⁠חָמֵ֥שׁ אַמּ֖וֹת מִ⁠פּ֑וֹ
2.note: Ezekiel is using **from here** and **from there** to mean “on each side.” You could indicate this explicitly in your translation if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [five cubits in width on each side]
The pronoun **its** refers to the nave, the large main room of the temple building. It may be helpful to clarify this for your readers. Alternate translation: [And he measured the length of the nave]

3.q: וְ⁠הַ⁠פֶּ֨תַח֙ שֵׁ֣שׁ אַמּ֔וֹת וְ⁠רֹ֥חַב הַ⁠פֶּ֖תַח שֶׁ֥בַע אַמּֽוֹת
3.note: This could mean: (1) that the opening itself was **six cubits** across and the walls on each side were **seven cubits** wide, Alternate translation: [and the opening itself, six cubits, and the walls on each side of the opening, seven cubits] or (2) that the opening itself was **six cubits** high and **seven cubits** wide. Alternate translation: [and the opening, six cubits high and seven cubits wide]

4.note: Here, **to the face of** represents being in front of **the nave**. Ezekiel means that this inner room was facing the nave, at its far end. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [facing the nave]

The man is using the possessive form to describe a **Holy** place that is characterized by being more holy than all other holy places. If a speaker of your language would not use the possessive form for this, you could express this idea in another way. Alternate translation: [the most holy place of all]

5.note: The implication is that **six cubits** was the thickness of **the wall of the house**. You could include this information if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [the wall of the house, which was six cubits thick]

Ezekiel is repeating the word **around** in order to intensify his expression of the idea that the side chambers went all the way around the house. If your language can repeat words for intensification, it would be appropriate to do that here in your translation. If not, your language may have another way of expressing the intensification. Alternate translation: [all the way around the house]

6.note: The phrase translated as **33 times** represents the standard written Hebrew text as we have it today. This reading, however, does not seem to make sense. Scholars have proposed that a scribe may have added a word or changed the order of the words. With a different order, it would say “three times and 30,” which seems to fit better the meaning of this passage. The UST follows that interpretation. You may want to follow the major translation in your area. Alternate translation: [three times, and 30]

6.q: צֵלָ֨ע אֶל צֵלָ֜ע שָׁל֧וֹשׁ וּ⁠שְׁלֹשִׁ֣ים פְּעָמִ֗ים
6.note: The implication is that the side chambers were built one above another in three stories. If you followed the alternate reading mentioned in the previous note, that means that there were 30 side chambers on each story. You could include this information if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [were built one above another in three stories, with 30 side chambers on each story]

This could mean: (1) ledges or supports that went out from the wall. The side chambers would be attached to these ledges. Alternate translation: [and supports coming out of the wall] (2) terraces or offsets that made the wall smaller as it went up. The side chambers would rest on top of these terraces or offsets. Alternate translation: [and offsets narrowing the wall]
See how you translated these same words, “around, around.” in the previous verse.

6.q: לִ⁠הְי֣וֹת אֲחוּזִ֑ים וְ⁠לֹֽא־יִהְי֥וּ אֲחוּזִ֖ים בְּ⁠קִ֥יר הַ⁠בָּֽיִת
6.note: The expressions **to be held** and **were not held** are passive verbal forms. If it would be unnatural to use those forms, you could express the ideas in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. If you must state what did the action, you could say that ledges in the wall held up the side chambers, but that the wall of the house itself did not hold them up. Alternate translation: [to hold the chambers up. And the wall of the house itself did not hold them up]

7.note: The pronoun **it** refers to the row of side chambers, which became wider as it went upward. It may be helpful to clarify this for your readers. Alternate translation: [And the row of side chambers widened and turned to above, to above]

Ezekiel is repeating the phrase **to above**, which means “upward,” in order to intensify his expression of the idea that the side chambers became wider at each higher story. If your language can repeat words for intensification, it would be appropriate to do that here in your translation. If not, your language may have another way of expressing the intensification. Alternate translation: [upward at each higher level for the side chambers]

This could refer to: (1) a staircase, probably a spiral one. There may have been one or two staircases, probably inside (or possibly outside) the front side chamber or chambers, Alternate translation: [for the staircases in the side chambers were going upward] or (2) a ramp, probably going all the way around the temple building. Alternate translation: [the ramp going around the house was going upward]
See how you translated these same words, “to above, to above” in the previous verse and “around, around” in verse 5. Alternate translation: [went upward all around the house]

This could mean: (1) that, since the side chambers were wider in the higher stories, the whole structure was wider at the top than at the bottom. This means that the higher side chambers would hang over the edges of the lower side chambers, Alternate translation: [the house was wider above than below] or (2) that the wall for the temple building became thinner as it went upwards. This way, each story of side chambers would end at the same point away from the walls, but the side chambers were deeper in higher stories. Alternate translation: [the house’s wall was thinner the higher it went, and the side chambers became deeper the higher they went]

Ezekiel is using the adjectives **lower**, **highest**, and **middle** as nouns to mean the three stories of side chambers. Your language may use adjectives in the same way. If not, you can translate these adjectives with equivalent phrases. Alternate translation: [he goes up the lower story to the highest story through the middle story]

The pronoun **he** does not refer to a specific person. It refers to anyone who went up from the lowest story of side chambers to the higher stories. It may be helpful to clarify this for your readers. Alternate translation: [And thus anyone would go up]

8.note: See how you translated these same words, “around, around.” in verse 5.

**The founded things of the side chambers** were a kind of foundation or raised platform on which the side chambers were built. If your readers would not be familiar with what these things are, you could use the name of a similar thing that your readers would recognize, or you could use a more general term. Alternate translation: [The foundations of the side chambers]

The expression **the fullness of the reed** means the full length of the measuring reed that the man was using, which was **six cubits**, or about 3.2 meters or 10.5 feet. If it would be helpful to your readers, you could express this measurement in modern measurements, either in the text or a footnote. Alternate translation: [the full length of the measuring reed]

This could mean: (1) what 40:5 means with “and a handbreadth.” It means that these are the long cubits, a handbreadth longer than normal cubits, Alternate translation: [which was six long cubits] or [which was six cubits and a handbreadth] or (2) a structure of some type, perhaps a terrace. Alternate translation: [six cubits, a terrace]

9.note: The expression **what was made rest** is a passive verbal form. If it would be unnatural to use that form, you could express the idea in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. If you must state who did the action, you could say that builders did it. Alternate translation: [And what the builders left open was a house of side rooms]

The expression **what was made rest** refers to a kind of open space that the builders left empty around the side chambers. If your readers would not be familiar with what this is, you could use the name of a similar thing that your readers would recognize, or you could use a more general term. Alternate translation: [And the open space left around them]

The phrase **a house of** is a translation of the standard written Hebrew text as we have it today. This reading, however, does not seem to make sense, since the author seems to be speaking about an area outside the side rooms. You may want to follow an alternative reading from the ancient Greek translation that uses the phrase “between the side rooms,” or you may want to follow the major translation in your area. Alternate translation: [between the side rooms that were to the house]

10.note: This could mean: (1) chambers that were connected to the wall at the edge of the open space measured here (these chambers are not mentioned elsewhere), Alternate translation: [chambers further away] or (2) the chambers for the priests mentioned 40:44. Alternate translation: [the chambers for the priests]
See how you translated these same words, “around, around.” in verse 5.

11.note: By **the thing being made rest**, Ezekiel means the open area beside the side chambers, which is the platform space around the temple building. You could indicate this explicitly in your translation if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [was to the open space]

11.q: פֶּ֤תַח אֶחָד֙ דֶּ֣רֶךְ הַ⁠צָּפ֔וֹן וּ⁠פֶ֥תַח אֶחָ֖ד לַ⁠דָּר֑וֹם
11.note: By **opening was the way of the**, Ezekiel means that the opening faced that direction. You could indicate this explicitly in your translation if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [One opening was toward the north, and one opening was toward the south]

This could mean: (1) that the platform (from 41:8) extended past the side rooms on each side a total of 5 cubits. In this case, this area is in addition to the open space of 20 cubits in 41:10, Alternate translation: [And the width of the open space created on top of the platform] or (2) that this open space is the same as the open space of 20 cubits in 41:10. This open space would have been distinguished in some way, perhaps by flooring or a line. The measurement of 20 cubits in 41:10 might include these 5 cubits, or these 5 cubits may be in addition to those 20 cubits. Alternate translation: [And the width of the inner part of the open space] or [And the open area that formed a ring within the open space]
See how you translated these same words, “around, around.” in verse 5.

12.note: Here, **to the face of** represents being in front of the courtyard. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [was in front of]

This could mean: (1) a courtyard or enclosed area, Alternate translation: [the enclosed area] or (2) a restricted area, one that only certain people could enter. Alternate translation: [the restricted area]

Here, **the sea** represents “the west.” The Mediterranean Sea was to the west of Israel. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [the side toward the west]
See how you translated these same words, “around, around.” in verse 5.

13.note: The pronoun **its** refers to the structure mentioned in the previous verse, not to the court. It may be helpful to clarify this for your readers. Alternate translation: [and the other structure and the walls of this structure]

14.note: Here, **face** represents “the front.” This measurement corresponds to measurement of the courtyard in front of the temple building and has already been mentioned in 40:47. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [And the width of the front of the house]

15.note: These **ledges** could mean: (1) shelves as in the UST or (2) a kind of gallery or terrace along the sides of the building. Alternate translation: [and its terraces]

Here, **to the face of** represents being in front of the courtyard. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [in front of]
See how you translated the same phrase, “from here and from there,” in 40:10.

This could be a list of: (1) three spaces. They would be the porch, the Holy Place, and the Most Holy Place. Alternate translation: [And the nave, the inner room, and the porch of the courtyard] or (2) two spaces. They would be the porch and the Holy Place. Alternate translation: [And the inner nave and the porch of courtyard]

16.note: See how you translated the similar expression, “shut windows,” in 40:16.

This could refer to: (1) the three spaces mentioned in the previous verse, Alternate translation: [for those three rooms] or (2) three stories or sets of ledges, Alternate translation: [for their three stories] or (3) three walls, leaving out the wall with the door in it. Alternate translation: [for the three walls]
See how you translated these same words, “around, around.” in verse 5.

The expression **being covered** is a passive verbal form. If it would be unnatural to use that form, you could express the idea in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. If you must state who did the action, you could say that builders did it. Alternate translation: [and the windows had coverings over them]

17.note: Ezekiel is using **upon from upon the opening** as a common expression of the culture to mean “above the opening.” If this phrase does not have that meaning for your readers, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [above the opening]

This could mean: (1) that the wood paneling covered everything inside, including the Most Holy Place (the **inner house**), and all the outside of the temple building as well, Alternate translation: [and up to the innermost room and on the outside of the temple building] or (2) the inner and outer main rooms of the temple, the Most Holy Place and the Holy Place. Alternate translation: [and up to the Most Holy Place and the Holy Place]
See how you translated these same words, “around, around.” in verse 5.

Ezekiel is leaving out some of the words that in many languages a sentence would need in order to be complete. You can supply these words from the context if that would be clearer in your language. Alternate translation: [on the inner side and on the outer side, all of it was paneled with wood according to exact measurements]

This could mean: (1) that the wood paneling was measured, either by Ezekiel’s guide or by the people who constructed the building. This probably means that each piece was the same size. Alternate translation: [each measured to the exact size] (2) that there were patterns at regular intervals on the wood paneling. These patterns are described in the following verses. Alternate translation: [and there were patterns on them]

18.note: The expression **made** is a passive verbal form. If it would be unnatural to use that form, you could express the idea in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. If you must state who did the action, you could say that workmen did it. Alternate translation: [And workmen decorated it with cherubs and palm trees]

Ezekiel assumes that readers will understand that by **between cherub to cherub** he means that the carved decorations alternated in a repeating pattern, so that each cherub had a palm tree on either side of it. You could say that explicitly if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [and a palm tree between each cherub and the next]

19.q: וּ⁠פְנֵ֨י אָדָ֤ם אֶל־הַ⁠תִּֽמֹרָה֙ מִ⁠פּ֔וֹ וּ⁠פְנֵֽי־כְפִ֥יר אֶל־הַ⁠תִּֽמֹרָ֖ה מִ⁠פּ֑וֹ
19.note: The implication is that the two faces described here belong to the cherubs mentioned in the previous verse. Since each cherub had two faces, one on each side, the man’s face and the young lion’s face belonged to the same cherub, looking in opposite directions toward the palm trees on either side. You could say that explicitly if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [And each cherub had the face of a man that looked toward the palm tree on one side, and the face of a young lion that looked toward the palm tree on the other side]
See how you translated these same words, “around, around.” in verse 5.

20.note: The expression **were made** is a passive verbal form. If it would be unnatural to use that form, you could express the idea in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. If you must state who did the action, you could say that workmen did it. Alternate translation: [workmen made the cherubs and the palm trees]

The phrase **the wall of the nave** is a translation of the standard written Hebrew text as we have it today. Some Hebrew scribes, however, marked the word translated as **the nave** as a possible error. The corrected text would simply be “and the wall.” You may want to follow this correction in your translation, or you may want to follow the major translation in your area. Alternate translation: [and the wall]

Ezekiel is leaving out some of the words that in many languages a sentence would need in order to be complete. You can supply these words from the context if that would be clearer in your language. Alternate translation: [and they were also made on the wall of the nave]

21.q: וּ⁠פְנֵ֣י הַ⁠קֹּ֔דֶשׁ הַ⁠מַּרְאֶ֖ה כַּ⁠מַּרְאֶֽה & הַ⁠מִּזְבֵּ֡חַ עֵ֣ץ שָׁלוֹשׁ֩ אַמּ֨וֹת
21.note: The punctuation and structure of these two verses represent the standard written Hebrew text as we have it today. This reading, however, may not seem to make sense. Scholars have proposed that a scribe may have added the wrong marks to the original consonants of the text, resulting in this structure. With different marks, it would say “And the face of the holy place, the appearance was according to the appearance of an altar of wood, which was three cubits” which may fit better the meaning of this passage. You may want to follow the major translation in your area. Alternate translation: [And in front of the holy place, there was something that looked like an altar, made out of wood, and three cubits]

If it would be more natural in your language, you may want to put the information about **The nave** with the information about **the doorpost**. Alternate translation: [The doorpost of the nave was square]

This could mean: (1) that a cross section of the **doorpost** had rectangular shape. Alternate translation: [was shaped with right angles] (2) that the **doorpost** created a rectangular opening. Alternate translation: [made a rectangular opening]

Here, **the face of ** represents being in front of the holy place. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [And in front of]

The implication is that using **according to the appearance** means that what Ezekiel has already described is exactly the same as these. You could include this information if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [had exactly the same appearance]

22.note: The phrase **and its length** is a translation of the standard written Hebrew text as we have it today. This reading, however, does not seem to make sense. You may want to follow an alternative reading from the ancient Greek translation which has “base,” or you may want to follow the major translation in your area. Alternate translation: [and its base]

Ezekiel is leaving out some of the words that in many languages a sentence would need in order to be complete. You can supply these words from the context if that would be clearer in your language. Alternate translation: [The altar was made of wood and]

The pronoun **he** refers to the man who was guiding Ezekiel and measuring the temple area. It may be helpful to clarify this for your readers. Alternate translation: [And the man who was guiding me spoke to me]

Here, **to the face of Yahweh** represents being in the presence of Yahweh. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [is in the presence of Yahweh]

23.note: The implication is that the **nave** and **the holy place** each had its own set of two doors. In this verse, “the holy place” means the inner room, the Holy of Holies. See the Chapter Introduction for further discussion of the doors as well as the different names for these special rooms. You could include this information if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [And the nave had two doors, and the holy inner room also had two doors]

24.q: וּ⁠שְׁתַּ֥יִם דְּלָת֖וֹת לַ⁠דְּלָת֑וֹת שְׁ֚תַּיִם מוּסַבּ֣וֹת דְּלָת֔וֹת שְׁ֚תַּיִם לְ⁠דֶ֣לֶת אֶחָ֔ת וּ⁠שְׁתֵּ֥י דְלָת֖וֹת לָ⁠אַחֶֽרֶת
24.note: The implication is that each of the **doors** mentioned in the previous verse was made of two panels, referred to as **turning doors**, that swung on hinges. You could include this information if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [And the doors each had two panels, two panels that turned on hinges: two panels for one door and two panels for the other door]

25.q: וַ⁠עֲשׂוּיָ֨ה אֲלֵי⁠הֶ֜ן אֶל דַּלְת֤וֹת הַֽ⁠הֵיכָל֙ כְּרוּבִ֣ים וְ⁠תִֽמֹרִ֔ים כַּ⁠אֲשֶׁ֥ר עֲשׂוּיִ֖ם לַ⁠קִּיר֑וֹת
25.note: The two uses of **made** are passive verbal forms. If it would be unnatural to use these forms, you could express the ideas in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. If you must state who did the action, you could say that workmen did it. Alternate translation: [And workmen made cherubs and palm trees on them, on the doors of the nave, just as they had made for the walls]

This could mean: (1) a canopy extended over the area just outside the porch, Alternate translation: [And a canopy of] or [And a wooden overhang] or (2) a railing or fence that blocked sight or entrance from the front of porch. Alternate translation: [And a railing of] or [And a fence of]

Here, **to the face of** represents being in front of the porch. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [on the front of the outside porch]

26.note: See how you translated the similar expression, “shut windows,” in 40:16.
See how you translated the same phrase, “from here and from there,” in 40:10. Alternate translation: [were on each side]
See how you translated these same phrases in 41:2. Alternate translation: [the sidewalls of the porch]

This could mean: (1) that the **side chambers** had **roofs** over them, just as the porch did, Alternate translation: [and side chambers of the house had roofs also] or (2) that the **side chambers** and **roofs** also had **palm trees** and **shut windows** decorating them. Alternate translation: [and also on the side chambers of the house and on the roofs]
